assumptions: Sufficient material yield per lot will allow single-vesicle assays on capture-positive particle-peak fractions.
Spike-in tracer chosen will behave comparably to endogenous intact EVs during capture and downstream single-vesicle workflows.
Assay platforms (droplet single-vesicle small-RNA profiling and low-input single-vesicle proteomics/lipidomics) can reach required sensitivity for capture-positive fractions.
biological_rationale: MISEV2023 and program rodent evidence motivate linking protected, membrane-associated cargo to EV identity and function. Prior lot-level bulk protected-cargo profiling is suggestive but cannot exclude co-isolated soluble complexes. Single-vesicle protected-cargo readout controlling for assay recovery (spike-in) and membrane protection will directly test whether a conserved, EV-contained multi-omic fingerprint exists across lots, resolving whether cargo consistency is an EV-associated manufacturing-controllable attribute.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Single-vesicle droplet small-RNA detection (UMI-tagged) combined with parallel single-vesicle-compatible luminal-protein detection and lipid-class context from particle-peak fractions; qualitative presence/absence across lots and sensitivity to detergent+protease.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Protected single-vesicle small-RNA + luminal-protein composite fingerprint
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Direct single-vesicle evidence that defined small-RNAs and detergent/protease-sensitive luminal proteins co-occur within intact capture-positive vesicles across lots would support an EV-associated cargo consistency attribute without asserting a single active molecule.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: High: analytical sensitivity and per-sample yield are key uncertainties; method development required.

edges.competing_explanation: Consistent bulk signals could reflect co-isolated soluble complexes or assay cross-reactivity rather than bona fide EV-contained cargo; single-vesicle-level membrane-protected detection is required to discriminate these possibilities.
edges.missing_experiment: Single-vesicle protected-cargo profiling with spike-in and detergent/protease controls across matched bounded EV fractions and secretome controls.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV2023 recommends protected-cargo linkage and program rodent results show activity but do not prove single-vesicle conserved cargo across manufacturing lots. Missing experiment: single-vesicle protected-cargo reproducibility across >=3 lots with spike-in controls.

nodes.statement: If intact, membrane-protected EVs carry conserved, protected small-RNAs and detergent-sensitive luminal proteins, then single-vesicle-level detection of these protected cargo elements will be reproducible across independent production lots and absent (or detergent-insensitive) in secretome-retaining concentrates.
If a single-vesicle protected-cargo fingerprint is reproducible across lots, it can serve as a qualitative lot-consistency metric to gate lots for downstream potency linkage and bridging studies.

competing_explanations: Bulk-protected cargo seen previously may be consistent across lots because of reproducible co-isolation of non-vesicular complexes (e.g., lipoproteins or protein aggregates) that survive protection assays.
Observed lot-to-lot conservation might reflect analytical harmonization rather than true biological conservation of EV-contained cargo.
dependencies: Availability of >=3 independent production lots from the same source-cell bank and matched processing
Spike-in tracer characterization and pre-validation in capture/single-vesicle formats
Analytical development resources for single-vesicle droplet assays and low-input proteomics/lipidomics
design_question: Daily question: Can a single-vesicle, spike-in-controlled protected-cargo multi-omic assay (intact immuno-capture → RNase/protease ± detergent → droplet single-vesicle small-RNA profiling paired with parallel single-vesicle proteomic/lipid readouts) reproducibly identify a conserved protected-cargo fingerprint across independent lots that is absent or unprotected in secretome-retaining concentrates?
expected_measurable_effect: A reproducible, qualitative single-vesicle fingerprint (presence of the predefined protected small-RNA subset + co-detected detergent-sensitive luminal protein(s) in capture-positive single vesicles and consistent lipid-class context in particle-peak fractions) observed across >=3 independent lots and absent or detergent-insensitive in secretome-retaining controls.

experiment.assay: Integrated single-vesicle protected-cargo workflow: (1) intact immuno-capture of particle-peak fractions; (2) split captured material into RNase/protease ± detergent conditions; (3) run droplet single-vesicle small-RNA sequencing (UMI-enabled) to detect protected small-RNAs at single-vesicle resolution and to quantify co-occurrence across vesicles; (4) in parallel, perform single-vesicle luminal-protein detection (proximity-based readout or microfluidic PRM from captured eluates) to test protease sensitivity; (5) perform targeted lipid-class LC-MS on matched particle-peak fractions for contextual signature; (6) analyze per-lot reproducibility of the composite fingerprint and compare to secretome controls.
experiment.comparator: Per lot: (A) bounded small-EV fraction vs (B) secretome-retaining concentrate processed identically. Within each, run RNase/protease ± detergent splits and include spike-in tracer. Positive control: characterized small EV prep; Negative controls: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted samples.
experiment.control: Spike-in tracer recovery per sample (must be recovered in capture-positive single-vesicles and show detergent/protease sensitivity); characterized small EV positive control processed in parallel; buffer-only negative controls; capture-compatibility checks for reagents/buffers.
dependencies: Establish per-sample spike-in tracer performance in capture and single-vesicle workflows before interpreting biological signals
Sufficient material yield from pilot lots to support single-vesicle droplet sequencing and low-input proteomics/lipidomics
Method development to adapt droplet single-vesicle small-RNA assays and single-vesicle-compatible proteomic readouts to low-biomass capture eluates
experiment.failure_criterion: Either (A) spike-in recovery validates assay performance but protected single-vesicle co-occurrence is not reproducibly observed across >=3 lots, or (B) protected signals are equally present in secretome controls (i.e., not EV-associated), or (C) spike-in fails to recover reproducibly, rendering the experiment inconclusive.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If falsified, conclude that no reproducible EV-associated protected multi-omic fingerprint exists across lots under current source/fractionation conditions; treat cargo composition as insufficiently consistent for lot-gating and prioritize alternative strategies (tighten fractionation, source-cell qualification, or secretome-centric product definitions).
experiment.hypothesis_tested: A conserved, membrane-protected multi-omic cargo fingerprint (protected small-RNAs + detergent-sensitive luminal protein(s) within the same intact capture-positive single vesicles and consistent lipid-class context) can be detected reproducibly across independent production lots and discriminates EV-enriched bounded fractions from secretome-retaining concentrates.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative reproducible detection (yes/no) across >=3 lots of: (A) a set of protected small-RNA species detected within intact, capture-positive single vesicles (not present after detergent+protease), and (B) co-detection of at least one protease-sensitive luminal protein within the same single vesicles; plus supportive consistent lipid-class context in particle-peak fractions. Spike-in recovery must validate assays.
experiment.question: Can a single-vesicle protected-cargo multi-omic assay (intact immuno-capture → RNase/protease ± detergent → droplet single-vesicle small-RNA profiling paired with parallel single-vesicle proteomic readout and lipid-class context) reproducibly identify a conserved protected-cargo fingerprint across independent lots that is absent or detergent-insensitive in secretome-retaining concentrates?
required_material: >=3 independent conditioned-medium production lots from the same source-cell bank/passage range processed identically into: (A) bounded small-EV fraction (program-defined) and (B) concentrated conditioned-medium secretome control
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) added to each sample prior to capture to control recovery
Immuno-capture reagents for intact EV surface markers (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5) configured for microfluidic/droplet capture compatibility
Microfluidic droplet single-vesicle small-RNA library prep reagents (UMI-enabled) and sequencing infrastructure or validated targeted single-vesicle RT panel

Parallel single-vesicle-compatible luminal protein readout (e.g., proximity-based luminal protein detection on captured vesicles or microfluidic single-vesicle PRM on eluates) with protease protection splits
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents for fraction-level particle counts
Protease (proteinase K) and RNase reagents and detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent) for protection/disruption controls
Reagents and platform for targeted lipid-class LC-MS on particle-peak fractions (sphingomyelin/PC/PE ratios) for contextual support
Buffers and capture-compatibility panels; negative controls (buffer-only) and positive controls (characterized small-EV prep processed in parallel)
secondary_readouts: Per-sample spike-in recovery percentage and detergent/protease sensitivity
Inter-lot similarity/clustering of single-vesicle small-RNA profiles (qualitative)
Presence/absence of the same protected signals in secretome-retaining concentrates (expected absent)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: Across >=3 independent production lots, capture-positive single-vesicle analyses reproducibly show the same protected small-RNA subset co-occurring with a detergent/protease-sensitive luminal protein within intact single vesicles (protected in -RNase/protease but lost with detergent + protease), and particle-peak lipid-class context is qualitatively consistent across lots; secretome-retaining controls lack this protected co-occurrence. Spike-in recovery confirms assay performance. Meeting this criterion supports adopting the protected single-vesicle fingerprint as a lot-consistency gate.

explicit_inferences: Single-vesicle level membrane protection of cargo (RNase/protease sensitivity ± detergent) more directly implicates EVs as the host of conserved cargo than bulk protected-cargo enrichment.
If the fingerprint is absent at single-vesicle level despite bulk signals, then bulk signatures likely reflect soluble co-isolates or assay artefacts.
falsification_criteria: Across ≥3 independent production lots, spike-in recovery validates assay performance but no reproducible co-occurrence of protected small-RNAs and detergent/protease-sensitive luminal proteins is observed at the single-vesicle level in capture-positive particle-peak fractions, or the same protected pattern is observed equivalently in secretome-retaining concentrates (i.e., the protected signal is not EV-associated).
If assay controls (spike-in recovery, detergent sensitivity of spike-in) fail reproducibly, the experiment is inconclusive and must be redesigned.
human_decisions_required: Select exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer (species/isotope label) and approve procurement
Approve allocation of >=3 pilot lots and required material for method development
Authorize specialized single-vesicle assay development resourcing and vendor/partner engagement
manufacturability_assessment: Medium risk/effort: single-vesicle droplet workflows and low-input proteomics/lipidomics are resource-intensive and require method development and spike-in controls, but a validated qualitative fingerprint would materially de-risk lot-to-lot comparability and focus upstream cell-bank and fractionation decisions.
manufacturing_rationale: A robust, reproducible single-vesicle protected-cargo fingerprint would enable non-numeric lot-comparability gating and focus CMC efforts (source-cell qualification, fractionation gate, stability envelopes) on preserving an EV-associated cargo signature rather than relying on bulk particle metrics that can be insensitive to membrane integrity or secretome co-isolates.
measurement_strategy: Develop and validate a single-vesicle protected-cargo workflow: intact immuno-capture of particle-peak fractions → split aliquots for (A) RNase/protease ± detergent treatment then microfluidic droplet single-vesicle small-RNA sequencing (or targeted single-vesicle RT) with unique molecular identifiers; (B) parallel single-vesicle-compatible proteomic readout (limited-target PRM on captured eluates or proximity-based luminal protein detection) ± protease; (C) particle-peak lipid-class profiling by targeted LC-MS for contextual support. Include exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer for per-sample recovery control and secretome-retaining matched controls.
novelty_statement: This hypothesis and experiment are novel because they test protected cargo at single-vesicle resolution using a spike-in-controlled, RNase/protease ± detergent split combined with droplet single-vesicle small-RNA profiling paired with single-vesicle-compatible luminal-protein detection and lipid-class context. Prior program experiments proposed bulk or fraction-level multi-omic protected profiling; none used single-vesicle droplet profiling to directly demonstrate that defined protected cargo co-occurs within individual intact EVs across manufacturing lots — a discriminating approach that can distinguish bona fide EV-contained cargo from co-isolated soluble complexes.
principal_risks: Insufficient sensitivity of single-vesicle assays on capture-positive fractions causing false negatives.
Spike-in tracer may not faithfully model endogenous EV behavior during capture and droplet workflows.
Detected conserved cargo could still reflect tightly bound non-vesicular complexes rather than bona fide intra-vesicular cargo if protection assays are incomplete.
proposed_potency_relationship: No potency claims asserted. If a reproducible protected-cargo fingerprint is found, it will be prioritized for subsequent potency linkage experiments (e.g., protected-fraction functional assays) but is not assumed to predict efficacy without follow-up.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: If supported, adopt a non-numeric lot-consistency attribute defined as a reproducible, membrane-protected single-vesicle multi-omic fingerprint: (A) a set of protected small-RNA species repeatedly observed within intact, capture-positive single vesicles; (B) at least one detergent/protease-sensitive luminal protein co-detected within the same single vesicles; and (C) a consistent lipid-class distribution in particle-peak fractions — to be used as a qualitative gate for lot advancement and prioritization of potency-linkage experiments.
title: Hypothesis SGL-001-CARGO-001: A conserved, membrane-protected single-vesicle multi-omic fingerprint (protected small-RNAs + detergent-sensitive luminal proteins + lipid-class context) will be detectable across independent production lots at the single-EV level and discriminate EV-associated cargo from variable secretome co-isolates
